reelection.rule: Rule: next even-year November for this House term. legislators-current.yaml ends the current term on 2027-01-03. The even-year November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file has no election day, so no day of the month is shown.

votes.question: On Passage — Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule issued by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to the “California State Nonroad Engine Pollution Control Standards; Commercial Harbor Craft Regulations; Notice of Decision” (H J RES 213)
votes.plain_language: This resolution would cancel the Environmental Protection Agency decision that partly let California tighten emissions rules for commercial harbor boats, including fishing boats. A Yea votes to cancel that decision. A Nay votes to leave it in place.

lobbying.bill_title: Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule issued by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to the "California State Nonroad Engine Pollution Control Standards; Commercial Harbor Craft Regulations; Notice of Decision".

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — To amend the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 to extend the time period for which certain regulations concerning the North Atlantic right whale are effective (H R 9436)
votes.plain_language: H.R. 9436 would move the deadline for new lobster- and crab-gear rules meant to protect North Atlantic right whales from 2028 to 2035. donor_industry.caption: From itemized individual contributions over $200 reported to the FEC, grouped by the donor's self-reported employer and occupation. Employer means where the donor works, not that the company gave money; corporations can't give directly to campaigns. Industry groups use simple keyword rules and may misclassify some donors.
donor_industry.cycle_rule: House filings use the 2026 two-year cycle.

stands_for.caption: Grouped by Congress.gov's official policy area. Shows how they voted, not why. Final-passage, amendment, and procedural votes can mean different things; read the note for each.
stands_for.scope: House roll calls 1–314 of 2026 (314 votes, January 6, 2026 to September 16, 2026), from the House Clerk.
stands_for.majority_rule: Party majority = the Yea/Nay side taken by most members of that party who voted Yea or Nay on that roll call, counted from the party code in the roll-call XML (all members, including ones no longer serving). Ties have no majority.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Combating Organized Retail Crime Act (H R 2853)
votes.bill_title: Combating Organized Retail Crime Act of 2025
votes.plain_language: This bill expands federal enforcement of criminal offenses related to organized retail and supply chain crime. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Law-Enforcement Innovate to De-Escalate Act (H R 2189)
votes.bill_title: To modernize Federal firearms laws to account for advancements in technology and less-than-lethal weapons, and for other purposes.
votes.plain_language: This bill removes less-than-lethal projectile devices (e.g., certain TASERs) from regulation under the Gun Control Act. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — KIDS Act (H R 7757)
votes.bill_title: KIDS Act
votes.plain_language: This bill requires specified online platforms to establish safeguards for minors. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Small Business Technological Advancement Act (H R 915)
votes.bill_title: Small Business Technological Advancement Act
votes.plain_language: This bill authorizes the Small Business Administration to finance, under its 7(a) loan program, business software or cloud computing services, including tools that use artificial intelligence. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Small Business Lending Fraud Prevention Act (H R 7401)
votes.bill_title: Small Business Lending Fraud Prevention Act
votes.plain_language: This bill requires Small Business Administration employees who take part in originating, reviewing, or approving agency loans to certify in writing that they have no conflict of interest with the loan and to disclose any conflict that arises later. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Small Business Innovation and Economic Security Act (S 3971)
votes.bill_title: Small Business Innovation and Economic Security Act
votes.plain_language: This bill reauthorizes through FY2031 and modifies the Small Business Innovation Research program, the Small Business Technology Transfer program, and related pilot programs. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — AI for Main Street Act (H R 5764)
votes.bill_title: AI for Main Street Act
votes.plain_language: This bill requires Small Business Development Centers to assist small businesses in evaluating artificial intelligence, including by providing best practices for using artificial intelligence and guidance about using artificial intelligence to plan for unexpected circumstances. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Main Street Parity Act (H R 5763)
votes.bill_title: Main Street Parity Act
votes.plain_language: This bill lessens the financing requirements for certain Small Business Administration loans to small businesses for plant acquisition, construction, conversion, or expansion, including the acquisition of land. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Adjourn (ADJOURN)
votes.plain_language: This was a motion to adjourn the House. A Yea votes to adjourn; a Nay votes to stay in session.

votes.question: Call of the House (QUORUM)
votes.plain_language: This was a quorum call, which records which members are present so the House can do business. It is not a vote on any measure. Members answer present; there is no Yea or Nay.

party_line.scope: House roll calls 1–314 of 2026 (314 votes, January 6, 2026 to September 16, 2026), from the House Clerk.

financial_disclosures.caption: Official House financial disclosure filings from the Clerk of the House. A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. This page links to the Clerk's copies and does not score anyone.

funding.heading: Disclosed campaign receipts
funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.

town_halls.note: There is no national town-hall dataset. Dates are not estimated.

disclosure_note: Disclosed contributions only; donors behind groups that do not report their own donors are not in this feed.
